claims.statement: The main-agent stack is composed in three bands: base scaffolding is appended first, caller middleware from the middleware= param is spliced in the middle, and profile/tail middleware is appended last.

Caller middleware is merged by name: an entry whose .name matches a base member replaces it in place preserving position, otherwise a new entry is inserted after the last core member so it precedes the profile/prompt-caching/memory tail.
A HarnessProfile can subtract members from the assembled stack via excluded_middleware, validated first to reject required scaffolding, then applied as a filter, then verified for coverage.

Each declarative SubAgent resolves its own model harness profile and independently assembles filesystem, summarization, patch-tool calls, profile extras, isolated-mode skills or forked parent skills, prompt caching, forked memory, two exclusion passes around spec middleware, coverage validation, and final tool exclusion; compilation then appends HITL when configured and unsupported-content filtering.
The auto-added general-purpose subagent is assembled with its own stack and inherits only caller middleware that overrides one of its default slots, not main-agent-specific middleware.

Declarative subagents inherit top-level tools, permissions, and interrupt_on only when their specs omit the corresponding field; their own permissions replace rather than extend parent rules, and compilation appends HumanInTheLoopMiddleware when the resolved interrupt configuration is non-empty.

Fork invocation supplies the parent's effective history plus a task preamble; declarative forks retain non-excluded parent state including private channels, compiled forks strip private state, and forked children are refused if they recursively invoke task.

Tool exclusion removes named tools from model requests and rejects attempts to call those names at the tool-call boundary; the implementation explicitly describes this as execution consistency rather than a security surface.

UnsupportedContentMiddleware filters only outgoing HumanMessage and ToolMessage content against the effective request model: it replaces explicitly unsupported multimodal blocks with text while retaining the original thread content, so a later compatible model can receive the original block.

Interrupt-mode filesystem permissions are converted during graph assembly into per-tool HumanInTheLoopMiddleware configurations; explicit interrupt_on entries override generated entries with the same tool name, while FilesystemMiddleware itself enforces deny rules rather than HITL.

Generated filesystem approval predicates distinguish exact and bulk tools: exact calls respect matching interrupt rules and deny precedence, while bulk calls conservatively gate intersecting subtrees, pathless searches, dot-root aliases, and glob patterns that can escape the supplied path; resolved symlink targets are considered when available.

Provider-payload tests verify that skill tool disclosure is inserted after the applicable read result without splitting tool-result batches or preceding queued user input, retains a stable request prefix, and relocates when compaction removes its original read anchor.

Filesystem permission tests cover conservative recursive-delete denial and generated interrupt handling for bulk delete, pathless and dot-root searches, glob escape patterns, and symlink-resolved paths.

The main core includes _ParentNotifierMiddleware between the optional synchronous SubAgentMiddleware and summarization middleware, so a novel caller middleware is inserted after that notifier as part of the core.

Main-agent prompt assembly places a caller-authored system prompt before the active harness profile's optional base prompt and suffix, and final compilation forwards that prompt, the processed caller tools, finalized middleware, and graph configuration to LangChain create_agent().
After main-stack assembly, private fields declared by surviving middleware state schemas are supplied to SubAgentMiddleware so synchronous task dispatch can withhold them from child state.

By default, a synchronous declarative subagent is isolated: it receives a delegated HumanMessage and non-excluded parent state, while unchanged returned state values are dropped to avoid reducer duplication and parallel-update conflicts.

Remote AsyncSubAgent specs are separated from inline task subagents during assembly and are handled by AsyncSubAgentMiddleware, while their approval and schema policy remains configured on the remote graph rather than inherited from the parent.

The automatic general-purpose subagent is added only when its profile is enabled and no inline subagent already uses the general-purpose name; when no synchronous subagent remains, the main stack has no SubAgentMiddleware and does not expose task.

Deep Agents creates model-aware summarization middleware for the main, declarative, and automatic general-purpose stacks; the summarization layer compacts over-threshold conversations, offloads the full history to the backend, and records its private per-invocation event and session state.

Prompt-caching assembly always adds a lazy Anthropic adapter that imports its delegate only for Anthropic requests, and conditionally adds Bedrock and Fireworks adapters when their integration packages are available.

MemoryMiddleware loads configured sources once into private state, injects formatted memory into the system message on model calls, and can mark the final system block with an Anthropic-only ephemeral cache-control breakpoint.

ModelRefusalMiddleware is appended after unsupported-content handling in the main, declarative, and automatic general-purpose stacks; a caller fallback middleware therefore handles a default main-agent refusal first, while synchronous task dispatch converts child refusal messages or refusal errors into a retry-oriented tool result.
